cards.explanation: The answer is livestock, friends. The Reubenites and Gadites had very large herds and flocks, and they saw that Jazer and Gilead were suitable for livestock (Numbers 32:1). When you own that many animals, every open stretch of land looks like a place to put them. I do the same thing with a bare counter and a fresh batch of dough.

The big ask is to have this land and not cross the Jordan. The Gadites and Reubenites say, “let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan.” (Numbers 32:5). Nice and polite on the front, and then the big request lands. I think I'd be a little nervous asking Moses, Israel's leader, for that one.

The answer is False, friends. Moses doesn't say yes to the Gadites and Reubenites, and he doesn't even say no yet. He asks, “Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?” (Numbers 32:6). When a leader answers your big ask with a question, you know you're about to have a long talk.

The answer is that they're discouraging the Israelites from crossing over. Moses asks the Gadites and Reubenites, “Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land that the LORD has given them?” (Numbers 32:7). Notice he doesn't say they said anything. He's talking about what their plan would do to everybody else.

The answer is their fathers. Moses says to the Gadites and Reubenites, “This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land.” (Numbers 32:8). He's pulling an old family story out of the closet. I bet nobody in that room wanted that one on the table.

The answer is True, bakers. Moses reminds the Gadites and Reubenites that their fathers discouraged Israel from entering the land, and he says, “So the anger of the LORD was kindled that day, and He swore an oath…” (Numbers 32:10). The fathers discouraged Israel from entering the land the LORD had given them, and the oath followed. That's why Moses is bringing it up now.

The answer is twenty years or older. The LORD says not one of the men twenty years of age or older who came out of Egypt will see the land, with two exceptions He names in the next verse (Numbers 32:11-12). Moses says it was because they did not follow Him wholeheartedly. The oath came with a clear age line.

The answer is Caleb and Joshua, friends. The LORD names “…Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite…” as one exception, and “…Joshua son of Nun…” as the other (Numbers 32:12). The reason given is that they did follow the LORD wholeheartedly. Out of that whole generation, those two made the short list.

The answer is forty years. Moses says the LORD “…made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation who had done evil in His sight was gone.” (Numbers 32:13). Forty years is a long time to wander. I think this part of the story is a heavy one.

The answer is wilderness, friends. Moses warns the Gadites and Reubenites that if they turn away from following Him, “…He will once again leave this people in the wilderness…” (Numbers 32:15). That word 'again' is doing a lot of work. Moses is reminding them where that road leads.

The answer is arm. The Gadites and Reubenites say, “But we will arm ourselves and be ready to go ahead of the Israelites…” (Numbers 32:17). That's the piece that changes the whole deal. They're not just staying put anymore.

The answer is True, bakers. The Gadites and Reubenites say, “We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has taken possession of his inheritance.” (Numbers 32:18). That's a big promise, and it covers every Israelite. Their little ones stay behind in the fortified cities while the men go.

The answer is that they may go home and the land is theirs. Moses tells the Gadites and Reubenites that when the land is subdued before the LORD, “…you may return and be free of obligation to the LORD and to Israel. And this land will belong to you as a possession before the LORD.” (Numbers 32:22). Work first, then home. Not bad for a promise that started with a lot of questions.

The answer is False, friends. Moses tells the Gadites and Reubenites, “But if you do not do this, you will certainly sin against the LORD…” and that their sin will find them out (Numbers 32:23). He's talking about what happens if they don't do what they promised. The words are very plain.

The answer is to do what they have promised. Moses says, “Build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, but do what you have promised.” (Numbers 32:24). He gives the Gadites and Reubenites the okay and then holds them to their word. Short and simple.

The answer is that they will do just as Moses commands, friends. The Gadites and Reubenites say, “Your servants will do just as our lord commands.” (Numbers 32:25). No arguing, no extra bargaining. They agree right there.

The answer is among the other tribes in Canaan. Moses tells the leaders, “But if they do not arm themselves and go across with you, then they must accept their possession among you in the land of Canaan.” (Numbers 32:30). So if the Gadites and Reubenites skip the fight, they don't keep the east side. They'd get their land with everyone else.

The answer is LORD, bakers. The Gadites and Reubenites say, “As the LORD has spoken to your servants, so we will do.” (Numbers 32:31). They're pointing past Moses to the One who spoke. That's a serious thing to promise.

The answer is Manasseh, friends. Moses gives the land to the Gadites, the Reubenites and “…the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph…” (Numbers 32:33). So it's only half of Manasseh that's named in this gift. It's a tribe cut in two.

The answer is that they drive them out. The text says the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh “…went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.” (Numbers 32:39). Machir was Manasseh's son. Gilead was the land these tribes had been eyeing since the start.

The answer is True, bakers. The text says, “So Moses gave Gilead to the clan of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settled there.” (Numbers 32:40). After the capture, they have a home. Quiet ending to that little story.

The answer is False, friends. Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and he “…called it Nobah, after his own name.” (Numbers 32:42). So Kenath got a brand new name. If I ever get a town, I'm calling it Dorin Heights.
